detail:
The Facial Pain Association reports that it has partnered with the National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) to launch the Facial Pain Registry, a global natural history study of neuropathic facial pain that includes trigeminal neuralgia (TN) along with other cranial neuralgias. The registry collects information through electronic surveys about the patient experience and disease progression, with data held confidentially in NORD's IAMRARE platform.

According to the association, registry data may be shared, with approval from the study's governing advisory board of researchers, medical professionals, association staff, and patient advocates, with individuals or institutions conducting research or clinical trials. The association describes the registry as a platform intended to advance understanding of facial pain conditions and to help drive medical discoveries and inform healthcare policy; TN is described in the source as the most common form of neuropathic facial pain.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about trigeminal neuralgia research and clinical trials.
summary: The Facial Pain Association reports launching a global Facial Pain Registry with NORD, a natural history study collecting patient experience and disease progression data for trigeminal neuralgia and other cranial neuralgias.
takeaways: the registry is a natural history study built on patient surveys
data sharing requires approval from the study's advisory board
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Trigeminal Neuralgia: a new registry tracking the patient experience
